topic: How Shazam knows the song (2002 story first)

lines.say: In twenty-oh-two, Shazam launched in Britain, and there was no app. You dialled two five eight oh, held your phone to the speaker, and got the song name back by text.
lines.show: In 2002, Shazam launched in Britain, and there was *no app.* You dialled *2580,* held your phone to the speaker, and got the song name [back by text.]

lines.say: Today, you catch a tiny clip of a song in a noisy café, and Shazam names it in seconds. How?
lines.show: Today, you catch a tiny clip of a song in a *noisy café,* and Shazam names it in seconds. [How?]

lines.say: First, it turns the sound into a map: low notes at the bottom, high notes at the top, time going across.
lines.show: First, it turns the sound into a *map:* low notes at the bottom, high notes at the top, [time going across.]

lines.say: Louder sounds glow brighter, and Shazam keeps only the brightest point in each patch. They look like stars in a night sky.
lines.show: Louder sounds glow *brighter,* and Shazam keeps only the brightest point in each patch. They look like [stars in a night sky.]

lines.say: The café noise adds a few extra stars and hides others, but enough of the pattern survives.
lines.show: The café noise adds a few extra stars and hides others, but [enough of the pattern survives.]

lines.say: It draws lines between pairs of stars, turning their pitches and timing into tiny codes. Together, those codes are the recording's fingerprint.
lines.show: It draws *lines between pairs of stars,* turning their pitches and timing into tiny codes. Together, those codes are the [recording's fingerprint.]

lines.say: Shazam has fingerprints for millions of songs, and looks for the one whose stars line up with yours.
lines.show: Shazam has fingerprints for *millions of songs,* and looks for the one whose stars [line up with yours.]

lines.say: So Shazam isn't recognising the tune. It's recognising one exact recording. That's why humming it won't work.
lines.show: So Shazam isn't recognising the tune. It's recognising *one exact recording.* [That's why humming it won't work.]
